search_intro: AxonBase offers four indexed search modalities: full-text, semantic vectors, geographic coordinates, and graph traversal. Each modality has its own index type and query operator in AxonQL.
search_ft_desc: The SEARCH index tokenizes text with a configurable analyzer (lowercase, stopwords, stemming) and indexes terms for BM25 (Best Matching 25) relevance search. The @@ operator activates the index, and search::score() and search::highlight() expose the relevance score and highlighted snippet in the projection.
search_ft_docker:
services:
  axonbase:
    image: axonbase
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
    environment:
      AXON_PATH: /data
      AXON_BIND: 0.0.0.0
      AXON_PORT: 8000
    volumes: [data:/data]
volumes: {data:}
search_vector_desc: The HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) index organizes vectors into a multi-level structure for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors; the closer to 1, the greater the semantic similarity. The WHERE field @@ $vector operator activates the vector index when an HNSW index is defined on the field.
search_vector_docker:
services:
  axonbase:
    image: axonbase
    ports: ["8000:8000"]
    environment:

      AXON_BIND: 0.0.0.0

    volumes: [vec_data:/data]
volumes: {vec_data:}
search_geo_desc: The GEO index indexes GeoJSON points for geographic proximity searches. geometry::point(lon, lat) builds a point and geo::distance() calculates distance in meters between two points using the haversine formula.

services:

search_graph_desc: AxonQL treats graph relations as first-class citizens. RELATE creates a directed edge between two record identifiers. Traversal uses -> (outgoing), <- (incoming), and <-> (both) arrows followed by the edge type and destination table.
search_graph_traditional:
-- Traditional SQL (multi-JOIN) for friends of friends
SELECT f2.name FROM person p1
JOIN friendship f1 ON f1.from_id = p1.id
JOIN person p2 ON p2.id = f1.to_id
JOIN friendship f2 ON f2.from_id = p2.id
JOIN person f2_name ON f2_name.id = f2.to_id
WHERE p1.name = 'Ana';

cluster_intro: AxonBase replicates state via Raft over TCP. Each group elects a leader; reads can be served by any replica, but every write must reach the leader and be confirmed by the quorum.
cluster_raft_desc: In a three-node cluster, the quorum is two active nodes. The leader appends the write to the Raft log and only responds after majority confirmation. A write sent to a follower fails with NOT_LEADER and provides leader and leader_address when a leader exists.
cluster_membership_desc: Membership changes are administrative writes and must be sent to the leader. The address is the Raft address in host:port format, not the HTTP port.

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/cluster/leave -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"address":"10.0.0.4:7000"}'

cluster_config_desc: Use the published Docker image with docker-compose for a three-node Raft cluster. Each node is identified by AXON_NODE_ID and binds Raft on port 7000. storage_intro: The server uses RocksDB (LSM-tree with ZSTD compression, bloom filters) as the default persistent backend, with fallback to memory for development and WAL legacy available.
storage_decision_desc: Use memory for testing and disposable data. The default is RocksDB: mature LSM-tree with leveled compaction, ZSTD compression, and bloom filters, used by Meta in production. WalBackend (WAL + snapshot) is available as a legacy alternative.

storage_backends.name: RocksDB (default)
storage_backends.desc: LSM-tree with leveled compaction, ZSTD compression, and bloom filters. Supports hundreds of millions of records with minimal heap. 243K inserts/s sustained in 50K batches. Built-in WAL + crash recovery.

storage_backends.name: Memory
storage_backends.desc: Data disappears when the process terminates. Useful for testing and CI.
storage_backends.code: docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=false -e AXON_PATH=memory axonbase/axonbase:latest

storage_backends.name: WAL (legacy)
storage_backends.desc: WAL + snapshot backend with fsync and crash recovery. Legacy alternative maintained for compatibility.
storage_backends.code: docker run -d --name axonbase -p 8000:8000 -e AXON_REQUIRE_AUTH=false -e AXON_PATH=/data-wal axonbase/axonbase:latest

storage_wal_desc: RocksDB stores data in SSTables (Sorted String Tables) organized in levels (leveled compaction). ZSTD compression reduces JSON records from ~200 B to about 25 B for repetitive textual data. Bloom filters avoid disk reads for absent keys. Writes go first to the RocksDB internal WAL and then to the memtable; when the memtable fills, it is flushed to level 0 and compacted to lower levels.
storage_recovery_desc: Each backend (RocksDB or WAL legacy) performs automatic recovery on directory open: RocksDB replays the internal WAL and applies pending compaction; the WAL backend reads the snapshot and replays the .wal, truncating incomplete records at the end.
storage_transaction_desc: BEGIN creates a transaction with pending changes and a per-key view captured on first read. COMMIT validates versions and read ranges against the versioned backend before applying changes; CANCEL discards them. SAVEPOINT, RELEASE, and ROLLBACK TO control checkpoints of pending writes and deletes.

storage_scenarios.title: Production: RocksDB Persistent
storage_scenarios.desc: The default. Use a directory for RocksDB: performance and reliability for tens of millions of records with minimal heap.

storage_scenarios.title: Local Disposable Test
storage_scenarios.desc: Start with --path memory when you don't need to preserve data after stopping the process.

storage_scenarios.title: WAL Legacy
storage_scenarios.desc: Use --path ./data-wal for the previous snapshot + WAL backend, maintained for compatibility.

storage_scenarios.title: Related Changes
storage_scenarios.desc: Group reads and writes in BEGIN and COMMIT when changes need to be confirmed together or discarded with CANCEL.

backup_intro: GET /export and POST /import transfer an AxonQL dump of the selected database. With S3 bucket and endpoint configured, the server also schedules cluster snapshot backups.
backup_export_desc: GET /export generates an AxonQL dump only for the namespace and database indicated by Axon-Ns and Axon-Db. POST /import executes that dump in the same scope. These endpoints are not the cluster snapshot format used by remote backup.
backup_s3_desc: Configure the bucket, credentials, and interval in the INI file or AXON_S3_* environment variables.
backup_s3_code:
s3_bucket = axonbase
s3_endpoint = https://s3.example.com
s3_prefix = backups
s3_access = ACCESS_KEY
s3_secret = SECRET_KEY
s3_interval = 60000
backup_minio_desc: MinIO can be used as a local S3 endpoint.
backup_minio_code:
s3_endpoint = http://127.0.0.1:9000
s3_bucket = axonbase
s3_access = minioadmin
s3_secret = minioadmin
backup_restore_desc: GET /export and POST /import operate on the namespace and database selected by Axon-Ns and Axon-Db. With require_auth active, these endpoints require authentication.
backup_restore_code:
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/export -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' > backup.axql
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/import -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data-binary @backup.axql
backup_schedule_desc: When s3_bucket and s3_endpoint are configured, the server starts periodic synchronization. s3_interval sets the interval in milliseconds; if zero or negative, the interval used is 60 seconds.
backup_failure_desc: A failed backup execution logs the error and returns failure without stopping the scheduler. On startup, the server tries to restore S3 backups only when local storage is empty.
backup_retention_desc: s3_retention determines how many recent remote backups are kept; default is 10 and values less than or equal to zero also use 10.
backup_encryption_desc: S3 upload uses streaming in 8 KiB blocks. AES-256-GCM encryption is applied only when s3_encrypt_key is configured.

backup_scenarios.title: Move a Database Between Environments
backup_scenarios.desc: Use GET /export and POST /import with Axon-Ns and Axon-Db to generate and execute an AxonQL dump of the selected database.

backup_scenarios.title: Retain Remote Cluster Snapshots
backup_scenarios.desc: Configure S3 to create periodic backups of the cluster state and use s3_retention to limit stored quantity.

backup_scenarios.title: Restore Cluster State
backup_scenarios.desc: With S3 configured, the server attempts to restore the cluster snapshot format on startup with empty local storage. POST /import remains reserved for per-database AxonQL dumps.

sql_overview_intro: AxonQL is the AxonBase query language. Statements operate on the session's namespace and database, using table records, graph relations, catalog, transactions, and real-time queries.
sql_overview_model_desc: Each record belongs to a table and receives an id field. CREATE accepts an identifier like person:ana; without an explicit key, the engine generates a UUID. RELATE creates a directed relationship between record identifiers.
sql_overview_lifecycle_desc: The parser transforms each statement into a syntax tree and the executor evaluates it in the session context. SELECT obtains a source, applies WHERE and permissions, sorts, limits, and projects the result. Writes update indexes, notify live queries, and can trigger table events.
sql_overview_ddl_desc: DEFINE creates catalog objects such as tables, fields, indexes, and users.
sql_overview_ddl_example:
DEFINE TABLE person SCHEMAFULL;
DEFINE FIELD name ON TABLE person TYPE string;
sql_overview_dml_desc: CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE, and RELATE modify records.
sql_overview_dml_example:
CREATE person:ana CONTENT {name: "Ana", age: 30};
UPDATE person:ana SET age = 31;
sql_overview_dql_desc: SELECT accepts projections, filters, JOIN, ordering, START, LIMIT, GROUP BY, FETCH, subqueries, and traversals. EXPLAIN shows the strategy chosen for a query.
sql_overview_dql_example: SELECT name FROM person WHERE age >= 18 ORDER BY name LIMIT 10;
sql_ddl_intro: DEFINE statements create and configure catalog objects. Tables, fields, analyzers, indexes, events, users, and access methods belong to the selected database catalog.
sql_ddl_schema_desc: SCHEMAFULL is stored as table metadata; the current implementation does not use it to reject undefined fields. Defined fields can apply DEFAULT, type coercion, ASSERT, and REFERENCES.

sql_ddl_statements.name: DEFINE TABLE
sql_ddl_statements.desc: Creates a SCHEMALESS or SCHEMAFULL table.

sql_ddl_statements.name: DEFINE FIELD
sql_ddl_statements.desc: Defines type, default, and validation for a field.
sql_ddl_statements.example: DEFINE FIELD age ON TABLE person TYPE number ASSERT $value >= 0;

sql_ddl_statements.name: DEFINE INDEX
sql_ddl_statements.desc: Creates a UNIQUE, COUNT, SEARCH, GEO, or HNSW index. SEARCH uses a previously defined analyzer.
sql_ddl_statements.example: DEFINE INDEX email ON TABLE person COLUMNS email UNIQUE;

sql_ddl_statements.name: DEFINE ANALYZER
sql_ddl_statements.desc: Configures normalization for a SEARCH index, with optional LOWERCASE, STOPWORDS, and STEMMING.
sql_ddl_statements.example:
DEFINE ANALYZER plain LOWERCASE;
DEFINE INDEX body_search ON TABLE article COLUMNS body SEARCH ANALYZER plain;

sql_ddl_statements.name: DEFINE USER
sql_ddl_statements.desc: Creates an identity at ROOT, NAMESPACE, or DATABASE scope.
sql_ddl_statements.example: DEFINE USER app ON DATABASE PASSWORD "password" ROLES writer;

sql_dml_intro: Use CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT, DELETE, and RELATE to modify records. CREATE and INSERT accept documents; UPDATE and UPSERT accept CONTENT, SET, MERGE, PATCH, or REPLACE.
sql_dml_semantics_desc: CREATE preserves the key of an explicit identifier and generates a UUID key when none is given. INSERT accepts an object or array of objects. UPDATE only changes records that match WHERE; UPSERT creates a record when none is found.

sql_dml_statements.name: CREATE
sql_dml_statements.desc: Creates a record with CONTENT or SET. An explicit identifier fixes the record key.
sql_dml_statements.example:
CREATE person:ana CONTENT {name: "Ana", age: 30};
CREATE person SET name = "Bob", age = 25;

sql_dml_statements.name: INSERT
sql_dml_statements.desc: Inserts an object or each object in an array into the specified table.

sql_dml_statements.name: UPDATE and UPSERT
sql_dml_statements.desc: UPDATE modifies existing records; UPSERT creates a record when the target produces no results.
sql_dml_statements.example:
UPDATE person:ana MERGE {age: 31};
UPSERT person:bob SET name = "Bob", age = 25;

sql_dml_statements.name: DELETE
sql_dml_statements.desc: Removes a record or the results of a filter.

sql_dml_statements.name: RELATE
sql_dml_statements.desc: Creates an edge between two records.

sql_dql_intro: SELECT reads tables, record identifiers, subqueries, and arrays. The query applies WHERE before ordering and the START/LIMIT window. Create a relationship with RELATE before using the label in a traversal.
sql_dql_planner_desc: EXPLAIN returns strategy, table, indexName when applicable, and examinedRows. The executor chooses UNIQUE_LOOKUP for equality on a field with a UNIQUE index; also recognizes FULLTEXT, GEO, VECTOR, and HYBRID in specific SELECT forms.

sql_dql_statements.name: Filter and Order
sql_dql_statements.desc: WHERE, ORDER BY, START, and LIMIT restrict the result.
sql_dql_statements.example: SELECT * FROM person WHERE age >= 18 ORDER BY age DESC LIMIT 10;

sql_dql_statements.name: Aggregation
sql_dql_statements.desc: GROUP BY works with count, sum, avg, min, and max aggregate calls.
sql_dql_statements.example: SELECT city, count() AS total FROM person GROUP BY city;

sql_dql_statements.name: JOIN
sql_dql_statements.desc: JOIN combines the FROM source with another source when ON contains a field equality. The flattened result uses table-prefixed keys.
sql_dql_statements.example: SELECT person.name, city.name FROM person JOIN city ON person.city_id = city.id;

sql_dql_statements.name: Links and Graph
sql_dql_statements.desc: RELATE creates a directed edge. The ->label->table projection returns destination records from the FROM record.

sql_dql_statements.name: Reverse and Bidirectional Traversal
sql_dql_statements.desc: Use <-label<-table to follow incoming edges and <->label<->table for both directions.
sql_dql_statements.example:
SELECT <-friend<-person FROM person:bob;
SELECT <->friend<->person FROM person:ana;

sql_dql_statements.name: Live Query
sql_dql_statements.desc: LIVE SELECT sends changes over the WebSocket connection.

sql_functions_intro: AxonQL includes built-in functions to transform values, inspect records, compute results, and access specialized resources. Names use namespaces like string::uppercase and vector::distance::euclidean; aggregations like count and avg are used in SELECT projections.
sql_functions_model_desc: A call receives expressions as arguments and returns an AxonQL value. Use RETURN to evaluate an expression without a source, use a SELECT projection or SELECT VALUE to evaluate it on each record, and use aggregations with GROUP BY to summarize groups.
sql_functions_scalar_desc: Scalar functions operate on their arguments at each evaluation. They can be nested, used in filters and ordering, or receive current row fields like string::uppercase(name).
sql_functions_aggregate_desc: count, sum, avg, min, and max summarize selected records. Without GROUP BY, the projection produces a summary of the entire source; with GROUP BY, it produces a summary for each grouping value.
sql_functions_aggregate_code: SELECT city, count() AS total, avg(age) AS average_age FROM person GROUP BY city;
sql_functions_discovery_desc: INFO FOR ROOT returns the names of registered built-in functions. Use this to confirm availability before assembling a query.
sql_functions_categories_desc: The namespaces below reflect the functions registered in the executor. Each family accepts the types indicated by the function and returns a value that can feed another expression, projection, or ordering.

sql_functions_categories.name: String
sql_functions_categories.desc: string::* transforms, combines, and examines text. concat, join, split, trim, slice, replace, slug, lowercase, uppercase, and matches return strings, arrays, or booleans.

sql_functions_categories.name: Math
sql_functions_categories.desc: math::* calculates rounding, power, logarithms, limits, and argument statistics. math::pi, math::e, and math::tau are parameterless constants; math::sum and math::mean compute over provided arguments.

sql_functions_categories.name: Arrays
sql_functions_categories.desc: array::* creates or reorganizes collections without modifying the original argument. distinct, union, intersect, difference, flatten, sort, slice, first, last, and len cover set operations, ordering, and access.

sql_functions_categories.name: Objects, Types, and Records
sql_functions_categories.desc: object::* exposes keys, values, and entries of objects. type::* converts values and tests types with type::is::*, while record::* extracts the key or table from a record identifier.

sql_functions_categories.name: Time and Randomness
sql_functions_categories.desc: time::now and now return the current instant; time::from::unix and time::from::millis construct datetimes, and time::year, month, day, hour, and other extractors read their parts. rand::* generates numbers, strings, UUIDs, or a random option.

sql_functions_categories.name: Cryptography, Encoding, and Values
sql_functions_categories.desc: crypto::* computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512 hashes. encoding::base64::* encodes and decodes UTF-8 text, and value::coalesce or value::default choose values when the first argument is NULL or NONE.

sql_functions_categories.name: Key-Value
sql_functions_categories.desc: kv::get, kv::set, kv::del, and kv::scan access the key-value store of the current namespace and database. Use them for direct pairs, separate from table records.

sql_functions_categories.name: Geometry and Vectors
sql_functions_categories.desc: geometry::* creates GeoJSON values, geo::* calculates distance, area, and containment, and vector::* calculates Euclidean or Manhattan distance and cosine similarity.

sql_functions_categories.name: Search
sql_functions_categories.desc: search::score() and search::highlight(field) only gain meaning in the projection of a text query with field @@ terms. score exposes the BM25 relevance of the row and highlight returns the highlighted text.

sql_functions_list.name: string::slug
sql_functions_list.desc: Normalizes text into a hyphen-separated identifier.

sql_functions_list.name: math::clamp
sql_functions_list.desc: Limits a number to the specified min and max range.

sql_functions_list.name: array::distinct
sql_functions_list.desc: Removes duplicate values, preserving the resulting collection.

sql_functions_list.name: object::keys
sql_functions_list.desc: Returns the keys of an object as an array.

sql_functions_list.name: type::is::number
sql_functions_list.desc: Tests whether the value is numeric.

sql_functions_list.name: record::id
sql_functions_list.desc: Extracts the key from a record identifier.

sql_functions_list.name: time::now and duration
sql_functions_list.desc: time::now returns the current instant, and duration literals like 1h represent AxonQL intervals.

sql_functions_list.name: crypto::sha256
sql_functions_list.desc: Computes the hexadecimal SHA-256 hash of text.

sql_functions_list.name: kv::set and kv::get
sql_functions_list.desc: Writes and reads a value by key name in the session's key-value space.

sql_functions_list.name: geo::distance and vector::distance::euclidean
sql_functions_list.desc: Calculate distance between GeoJSON points and between numeric vectors, respectively.

sql_functions_list.name: search::score and search::highlight
sql_functions_list.desc: Project relevance score and highlighted snippet from an indexed text match.
sql_functions_list.example: SELECT title, search::score() AS score, search::highlight(body) AS snippet FROM article WHERE body @@ "cat" ORDER BY search::score() DESC;

sql_operators_intro: AxonQL expressions offer arithmetic, comparison, logical, collection, text, and traversal operators.
sql_operators_notes_desc: AND and &&, as well as OR and ||, are equivalent. IN tests whether the left value is in the right value; CONTAINS tests the opposite direction. @@ represents text matching; it uses a SEARCH index when WHERE has the form field @@ text and an applicable index exists.

sql_operators_list.name: logical and
sql_operators_list.desc: Requires both expressions to be true.

sql_operators_list.name: belongs to
sql_operators_list.desc: Checks if the left value is in the right array or result.

sql_operators_list.name: contains
sql_operators_list.desc: Checks if the left collection or text contains the right value.

sql_operators_list.name: coalescence
sql_operators_list.desc: Uses the right operand when the left is NULL or NONE.

sql_time_travel_intro: Time travel reads values kept in the WAL backend ledger. It is a point-in-time value view, not a general SQL command replay: only changes recorded in the ledger after history was enabled can appear in the past.
sql_time_travel_as_of_desc: AT accepts TIMESTAMP with a datetime, ISO 8601 string, or numeric value in milliseconds since Unix Epoch. Use the timestamp captured before the change you want to compare.
sql_time_travel_as_of_go: rows, err := axon.Query("SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:00:00Z')", nil)
sql_time_travel_as_of_rust: let rows = axon.query("SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:00:00Z')", None).await?;
sql_time_travel_between_desc: The parser recognizes BEFORE (STATEMENT => ...), but the current engine does not maintain or resolve a timeline by statement identifier.
sql_time_travel_between_sql:
SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:00:00Z');
SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:05:00Z');
sql_time_travel_between_java:
var before = axon.query("SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:00:00Z')");
var after = axon.query("SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T12:05:00Z')");
sql_time_travel_diff_desc: There is no clause to compute differences between historical versions. LIVE SELECT DIFF produces JSON Patch only for real-time changes.
http_overview_intro: The server exposes REST, JSON-RPC over HTTP and WebSocket, GraphQL, and MCP (Model Context Protocol).
http_overview_rest_desc: Send AxonQL to the /sql endpoint with namespace and database in headers.
http_overview_rest_example: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data 'SELECT * FROM person'
http_overview_rpc_desc: POST /rpc receives the JSON-RPC envelope; the HTTP session does not persist between requests.
http_overview_rpc_example: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"id":1,"method":"query","params":["SELECT * FROM person"]}'
http_overview_graphql_desc: POST /graphql translates GraphQL queries to AxonQL from the catalog.
http_rest_intro: The /sql endpoint executes AxonQL. Axon-Ns and Axon-Db define the target database.
http_rest_query_desc: Send a query in the request body.
http_rest_query_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data 'SELECT * FROM person'
http_rest_exec_desc: CREATE and UPDATE use the same /sql endpoint.
http_rest_exec_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data 'CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana"}'
http_rest_exec_node: await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql', {method: 'POST', headers: {'Axon-Ns':'test','Axon-Db':'dev'}, body: 'CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana"}'});
http_rest_stream_desc: Live query notifications are delivered via WebSocket, not REST.
http_rest_stream_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql --data 'LIVE SELECT * FROM person DIFF'
http_rest_stream_go: // Use axon.Live to receive WebSocket notifications.
http_rpc_intro: JSON-RPC is available on POST /rpc and WebSocket /rpc/ws.
http_rpc_example_desc: The current protocol version is 1; on WebSocket, read the hello frame first.
http_rpc_example_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"id":1,"method":"query","version":1,"params":["SELECT * FROM person"]}'
http_graphql_intro: POST /graphql creates the schema from catalog tables and translates simple queries to AxonQL.
http_graphql_queries_desc: Query a table in the database selected by headers. The endpoint also responds to __schema introspection.
http_graphql_query_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data '{"query":"{ person { id name } }"}'
http_graphql_mutations_desc: The current GraphQL endpoint does not execute mutations. Use POST /sql or JSON-RPC to write data.
http_graphql_mutation_example:
# GraphQL mutations are not supported.
CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana"};
http_graphql_mutation_curl: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/sql -H 'Axon-Ns: test' -H 'Axon-Db: dev' --data 'CREATE person CONTENT {name: "Ana"}'
http_graphql_subscriptions_desc: Real-time transport is WebSocket JSON-RPC with live queries; there is no separate GraphQL subscription endpoint.
http_mcp_intro: AxonBase exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over SSE (Server-Sent Events) at /mcp. AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, and bolt.diy connect to discover tables, query data, and retrieve schema information using structured tools, not arbitrary AxonQL.
http_mcp_tools_desc: The MCP server exposes two read-only tools by default. Use tools/list to discover them.
http_mcp_tools_call_desc: Invoke axon_select to read up to 100 rows from a table, or axon_info to inspect the database catalog. Both tools respect Data Rules, row permissions, and authentication scope.
http_mcp_resources_desc: resources/list provides one resource per table in the selected namespace and database, using the axon:// URI scheme.
http_mcp_config_desc: Open GET /mcp/sse to start an SSE session. The server responds with an endpoint event containing the POST /mcp/message URL for the session. All subsequent tool calls use that URL.
http_mcp_config_example:
# Start SSE session (long-lived connection)
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/sse

# Response contains:
event: endpoint
data: /mcp/message?session_id=<uuid>

# Send tool calls to the returned URL:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/message?session_id=<uuid> \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
http_mcp_clients_desc: Connect AxonBase MCP to your preferred AI coding agent. Below are the configuration snippets for each supported client.
http_mcp_use_cases_intro: These scenarios show how an AI coding agent uses AxonBase MCP to interact with the database during development and operations.

http_mcp_use_cases.title: Schema Discovery and Query
http_mcp_use_cases.scenario: An AI agent needs to understand the database schema before writing application code. It connects to MCP, discovers tables via resources/list, inspects the catalog with axon_info, and samples data with axon_select.
http_mcp_use_cases.code:
List all tables in the current database.
Then describe the structure of the 'orders' table.
Finally, show me the 5 most recent orders.

http_mcp_use_cases.title: Debugging a Slow Query
http_mcp_use_cases.scenario: A developer reports that a query is slow. The agent uses axon_select to inspect table sizes, uses axon_info to check indexes, and analyzes the data distribution before suggesting an index.
http_mcp_use_cases.code:
Check how many rows are in the 'orders' table.
What indexes are defined on it?
Show me the distribution of order_status values.

http_mcp_use_cases.title: Auditing Data Access
http_mcp_use_cases.scenario: A compliance officer needs to verify that sensitive data is properly protected. The agent connects to MCP, inspects Data Rules, and confirms that PII fields are masked and access is scoped.
http_mcp_use_cases.code:
Show me the table definitions and check which fields have Data Rules or permissions defined.
Verify that the 'cpf' field is masked for non-admin users.

http_mcp_limitations_desc: The current MCP implementation has the following constraints:
http_mcp_limitations_list: Read-only by default: axon_query, axon_create, and axon_export are not exposed. Only axon_select and axon_info are available.
No prompts support: prompts/list is not implemented.
Authentication: when require_auth is enabled, clients must send Authorization: Bearer <token> headers on the SSE connection and every message POST.
Single session per SSE connection: each SSE connection creates one MCP session. The session is tied to the HTTP connection lifecycle.
No cursor-based pagination: axon_select returns up to 100 rows. Larger result sets require multiple queries.
No table name validation beyond regex: the server validates table names with a simple pattern, not against the full catalog.
auth_intro: The server uses JWT, scoped users, and table permissions.
auth_jwt_desc: With require_auth active, send Authorization: Bearer <token> in HTTP requests.
auth_signin_desc: SDKs authenticate the WebSocket session with signin and authenticate.
auth_signin_node:
const token = await axon.signin('root', 'root');
await axon.authenticate(token);
auth_cert_desc: Certificate login uses mTLS or the certificate.begin and certificate.complete RPC flow.
auth_temp_desc: certificate.complete returns a temporary credential after validating the challenge and certificate chain.
auth_scopes_desc: Users can have ROOT, NAMESPACE, or DATABASE scope.
auth_scopes_code:
DEFINE USER app ON DATABASE PASSWORD "password" ROLES writer;
DEFINE ACCESS app_login ON DATABASE;
auth_permissions_desc: PERMISSIONS FOR controls operations per record.
auth_permissions_code: DEFINE TABLE person PERMISSIONS FOR SELECT TRUE, FOR CREATE WHERE $token.scope = "ROOT", FOR DELETE FALSE;
cert_intro: Certificate authentication combines a JKS trust anchor, a user linked to the store, and one of two proof methods: mTLS transport or JSON-RPC challenge.
cert_root_desc: CREATE JKS is an administrative runtime operation and only a ROOT-scoped authenticated session can execute it.
cert_root_flow_desc: A ROOT administrator imports the authorities into the JKS and executes CREATE JKS.
cert_truststore_title: 2. Build and Import the JKS Truststore
cert_truststore_desc: Create a JKS containing the CA certificates that can issue the accepted client certificates.
cert_register_desc: In a ROOT session, CREATE JKS loads the file and associates it with a store name.
cert_oid_desc: COLLECT USER BY OID reads values from the certificate's subject distinguished name (DN).
cert_collector_flow_desc: Use OID when the identity is in specific known subject DN attributes, declaring them in preference order.
cert_oid_code: CREATE JKS company PATH "/etc/axonbase/truststores/company.jks" PASSWORD "changeit" COLLECT USER BY OID "2.5.4.5", "2.16.76.1.3.1";
cert_icp_desc: COLLECT USER BY ICPBRASIL selects the built-in CPF or CNPJ collection at the certificate login endpoint.
cert_user_desc: DEFINE USER associates the identity with the registered store name via CERTIFICATE.
cert_user_code: DEFINE USER 12345678901 ON DATABASE CERTIFICATE icp_brasil ROLES writer;
cert_mtls_desc: tls_cert and tls_key configure the server's PKCS12 keystore.
cert_proof_desc: certificate.begin returns an id, a 32-byte Base64URL challenge, and expires_at, 30 seconds ahead.
cert_credential_desc: After validating the chain, signature, and DEFINE USER binding, certificate.complete or mTLS login issues an axontc_ opaque credential.
cert_temp_flow_desc: Complete mTLS login or certificate.complete, use the axontc_ credential with the same user in signin, and authenticate the session with the returned JWT.

faq_intro: Practical answers for development, operations, and integration. Each answer describes the behavior available in the current implementation.

faq_items.a: It is a multi-model database in Java 21+ with AxonQL, documents, graphs, key-value operations, and memory or RocksDB storage. The server offers HTTP, WebSocket JSON-RPC, JDBC, basic GraphQL, and MCP (Model Context Protocol).

The server uses 127.0.0.1:8000 by default for HTTP and WebSocket. When TLS is configured, the main port serves HTTPS/WSS; use plain_port to keep an additional non-TLS WS port for development and local JDBC tools.

faq_items.q: How do I choose between memory and WAL?
faq_items.a: Use path = memory for quick tests and disposable data. The default is RocksDB (path = data): mature LSM-tree with leveled compaction, ZSTD compression, and bloom filters, supporting hundreds of millions of records with minimal heap. The legacy WalBackend (WAL + snapshot) is also available.

On a versioned WAL backend, each write records the document state. Query a historical view with SELECT * FROM person AT (TIMESTAMP => '2026-08-27T00:00:00Z'). Before using in production, define a retention policy consistent with your update volume and audit needs.

The cluster uses Raft over TCP. Writes must go through the leader and are only confirmed with quorum. A follower returns NOT_LEADER; clients can reconnect to the informed leader address. Use the included Docker Compose as a three-node topology reference.

For WebSocket, call signin with user and password, then authenticate with the returned JWT. For HTTP without session, send Authorization: Bearer <token> along with Axon-Ns and Axon-Db headers. Users can be ROOT, NAMESPACE, or DATABASE scope.

faq_items.q: How does digital certificate login work?
faq_items.a: Register a JKS truststore and a user collection strategy, for example COLLECT USER BY ICPBRASIL. The certificate endpoint validates the chain, extracts CPF or CNPJ when applicable, and issues a temporary credential.

faq_items.q: Does the JDBC driver use PostgreSQL protocol?
faq_items.a: No. axonbase-jdbc implements JDBC over WebSocket JSON-RPC and uses jdbc:axonbase:ws:// or jdbc:axonbase:wss:// URLs.

faq_items.q: How do I backup and restore?
faq_items.a: Use GET /export to produce an AxonQL dump and POST /import to restore it in the selected namespace and database. For remote copies, configure an S3-compatible endpoint like MinIO.

faq_items.q: Does GraphQL support mutations and subscriptions?
faq_items.a: Not in the current implementation. POST /graphql resolves simple table selections and lightweight introspection. For writes, use AxonQL, POST /table/{table}, or JSON-RPC.

faq_items.q: What should I monitor in production?
faq_items.a: Monitor /health for process availability, /ready for readiness and quorum, /status for Raft role and leadership, and /metrics for Prometheus metrics.

sdk_php_intro: The PHP SDK is a synchronous PHP 8.1+ WebSocket client. It receives the server hello frame when connecting and sends JSON-RPC protocol version 1 with every request.
sdk_php_connection_desc: connect opens the WebSocket connection. use selects its namespace and database, signin returns and stores a token, and authenticate accepts either that token or one obtained elsewhere.
sdk_php_query_desc: query executes AxonQL. Pass an associative array as the optional second argument to bind AxonQL variables by name.
sdk_php_crud_desc: The helpers return decoded JSON results. select and delete accept an optional filter as their second argument; create, update, and upsert accept a table or record target, while insert accepts a table.
sdk_php_session_desc: ping returns a boolean, version returns the server version, namespace and database expose the selected scope, and hello exposes the first server frame. Always close the transport when finished.
sdk_php_errors_desc: All SDK errors extend AxonBase\Error. RPC error codes are mapped to AuthError, ConflictError, NotLeaderError, NoQuorumError, RateLimitError, and ProtocolMismatchError. NotLeaderError also exposes leader and leaderAddress; ProtocolMismatchError exposes protocol and serverVersion.
sdk_php_migration_desc: Migrator loads one .axql file or all .axql files in a directory in lexical order. Migration exposes version, name, path, checksum, and sql. ensureTable creates the _migration tracking table; applied returns its version-to-checksum map; status marks each loaded migration as applied. up runs pending migrations once, records their SHA-256 checksum, and fails when an applied file changes. onBefore and onAfter run around every pending migration.
sdk_ruby_intro: The Ruby SDK is a synchronous Ruby 2.6+ WebSocket client. Rails applications can construct Client with a custom transport that uses their chosen WebSocket stack.
sdk_ruby_connection_desc: Client.connect opens the WebSocket connection. use selects its namespace and database, signin returns and stores a token, and authenticate accepts either that token or one obtained elsewhere.

require "axonbase"

axon = AxonBase::Client.connect("ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws")
axon.use("test", "dev")
token = axon.signin("root", "root")
axon.authenticate(token)
sdk_ruby_query_desc: query executes AxonQL. Pass a Hash as the optional second argument to bind AxonQL variables by name.

updated = axon.update("person:ana", { "age" => 31 })
upserted = axon.upsert("person:bia", { "name" => "Bia", "age" => 28 })
deleted = axon.delete("person", "age < 18")
sdk_ruby_session_desc: ping returns a decoded result, version returns the server version, and the namespace, database, and hello readers expose connection state. Always close the transport when finished.

sdk_ruby_errors_desc: All SDK errors inherit from AxonBase::Error. RPC error codes are mapped to AuthError, ConflictError, NotLeaderError, NoQuorumError, RateLimitError, and ProtocolMismatchError. begin

rescue AxonBase::NotLeaderError => error

sdk_ruby_migration_desc: Migrator loads one .axql file or all .axql files in a directory in lexical order. Migration exposes version, name, path, checksum, and sql. ensure_table creates the _migration tracking table; applied returns its version-to-checksum map; status marks each loaded migration as applied. up runs pending migrations once, records their SHA-256 checksum, and fails when an applied file changes. on_before and on_after run around every pending migration.
sdk_ruby_migration_code:
migrator = AxonBase::Migrator.new(axon)
migrator.on_before { |migration| Rails.logger.info("Applying #{migration.name}") }
migrator.on_after { |migration| Rails.logger.info("Applied #{migration.name}") }

migrator.ensure_table
migrations = migrator.load(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s)
checksums = migrator.applied
status = migrator.status(Rails.root.join("db/axonbase_migrations").to_s)

search_overview_subtitle: AxonBase replaces Elasticsearch for BM25 full-text search, Qdrant or Pinecone for HNSW vector search, dedicated geo services like MongoDB Geo or Elastic Geo, graph databases like Neo4j or Dgraph, and analytical column stores like ClickHouse, all within a single database with native SQL.
search_overview_diagram_alt: Diagram of AxonBase's five search engines: BM25 full-text, HNSW vector, geo radius, graph traversal, and columnar index
search_overview_replace_desc: Most architectures combine Elasticsearch for text search, Qdrant or Pinecone for vector similarity, MongoDB Geo or Elastic Geo for location queries, Neo4j or Dgraph for graph traversal, and ClickHouse for analytical aggregation. AxonBase eliminates all these external dependencies with native SQL engines implementing BM25, HNSW, GEO, graph traversal, and columnar index, reducing infrastructure complexity and operational cost.
search_overview_ft_desc: Industry-standard BM25 ranking with tokenization, stopword removal, and stemming via DEFINE ANALYZER and DEFINE INDEX SEARCH.
search_overview_vector_desc: Hierarchical Navigable Small World index for approximate nearest neighbor search. Configure DIMENSION and DIST per index.
search_overview_geo_desc: R-Tree spatial index on GeoJSON points with real-time distance queries and bounding box filtering.
search_overview_graph_desc: Directed adjacency edges with RELATE and single-line AxonQL traversal for friend-of-friend and path queries.
search_overview_columnar_desc: Columnar index with sortable value encoding for direct aggregation of count, sum, avg, min, and max without loading documents from the main KV store. Prefix scan on CI| prefix.
search_ft_subtitle: Replace Elasticsearch: native BM25 text search with analysis pipelines, inverted indexes, and ranked results, all in SQL.
search_ft_scenario_desc: A content management system stores thousands of articles and needs to search by title and body with relevance ranking. AxonBase replaces a separate Elasticsearch cluster with a native BM25 search engine.
search_ft_bm25_desc: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is the industry-standard ranking function used by Elasticsearch and Lucene. It scores documents by term frequency (how many times a term appears in the document), inverse document frequency (how rare the term is in the corpus), and field-length normalization (shorter fields are more significant). AxonBase implements BM25 natively with configurable k1 and b parameters.
search_ft_index_desc: Define an analyzer with tokenization, stopword filtering, and stemming rules, then create a search index on the relevant columns. The analyzer processes text identically during indexing and querying.
search_ft_index_code:
DEFINE ANALYZER my_analyzer
  WITH tokenizer = 'standard',
       filters  = ['lowercase', 'stopwords', 'stemmer'];

DEFINE INDEX SEARCH articles_idx
  ON TABLE articles
  WITH analyzer = my_analyzer,
       COLUMNS  = (title, body);
search_ft_query_desc: Use the double @@ operator to activate text search. The search::score() function returns the BM25 relevance score, which you can use in ORDER BY and WHERE.
search_ft_query_code: SELECT id, title, search::score() AS relevance FROM articles WHERE body @@ 'machine learning' ORDER BY relevance DESC LIMIT 20;

search_vector_subtitle: Replace Qdrant and Pinecone: native HNSW nearest neighbor search with configurable dimensions and distance functions.
search_vector_scenario_desc: An AI agent built with LangChain embeds product descriptions into 384-dimensional vectors. When a user asks about similar items, the agent needs semantic search across millions of embeddings. AxonBase replaces a dedicated vector database with a native HNSW index.
search_vector_hnsw_desc: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) builds a multi-layer graph where each layer is a downsampled version of the layer below. Search starts at the top layer and descends to finer granularity, achieving approximate nearest neighbor search in O(log n) time.
search_vector_index_code: DEFINE INDEX knowledge_embedding ON TABLE knowledge_chunks COLUMNS embedding HNSW DIMENSION 384 DIST cos;
search_vector_query_desc: Use vector::similarity::cosine() para calcular a distancia semantica entre uma coluna de embedding e um vetor de consulta. Ordene por pontuacao e limite aos vizinhos mais proximos.
search_vector_query_code: SELECT id, content, vector::distance::cosine(embedding, [0.11, 0.44, 0.76, 0.35]) AS distance FROM knowledge_chunks ORDER BY distance ASC LIMIT 5;
search_vector_hybrid_desc: Combine BM25 filtering with vector similarity ranking in a single query. WHERE filters candidates by full-text, while ORDER BY ranks by vector distance.
search_vector_hybrid_code: SELECT id, content, vector::distance::cosine(embedding, [0.11, 0.44, 0.76, 0.35]) AS distance FROM knowledge_chunks WHERE content @@ "vector search" ORDER BY distance ASC LIMIT 5;

search_geo_scenario_desc: A food delivery app needs to find restaurants within a 5 km radius of the user's location, ordered by distance. AxonBase replaces a dedicated geo service like MongoDB Geo or Elastic Geo with a native R-Tree index.

search_graph_subtitle: Replace Neo4j and Dgraph: native directed adjacency edges with single-line AxonQL traversal, no JOINs.
search_graph_scenario_desc: A social network needs to find friends of friends for a recommendation engine. In a traditional relational database, this requires 4 JOINs. AxonBase replaces a dedicated graph database with native adjacency edges and concise traversal language.
search_graph_model_desc: Use RELATE to create directed edges between records. Each edge has a source, destination, and label, creating a persistent adjacency structure that AxonBase traverses without JOINs.
search_graph_traditional_desc: Em um modelo relacional padrao, encontrar amigos de amigos requer quatro JOINs entre as tabelas de usuarios e amizades. A consulta se torna cada vez mais complexa para travessias mais profundas.

FROM users u1
JOIN friendships f1 ON u1.id = f1.user_id
JOIN friendships f2 ON f1.friend_id = f2.user_id
JOIN users u3 ON f2.friend_id = u3.id
WHERE u1.id = 1;
search_graph_axonql_desc: O AxonQL percorre arestas com o operador de seta ->rotulo->. A mesma consulta de amigos de amigos se torna uma linha unica, sem JOINs, sem tabelas intermediarias, sem complexidade de ORM.

SELECT count(), sum(age), avg(age) FROM users;
search_columnar_subtitle: The columnar index accelerates analytical queries (count, sum, avg, min, max) without loading documents from the main KV store. Replaces dedicated column stores like ClickHouse for aggregation within AxonBase.
search_columnar_what_desc: The columnar index stores each column separately with sortable value encoding (null, bool, long, double, string, array, object). The key follows the format CI|{ns}|{db}|{table}|{index}|{column}|{typeByte}{encodedData}{rowKey}. This allows scanning column values without deserializing entire documents.
search_columnar_advantages_list: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX without loading documents: aggregation reads only the indexed column
Less memory and CPU: values stored in sortable binary format, no JSON
Efficient linear scan: CI| prefix is contiguous in RocksDB, no random seeks
ZSTD compression in RocksDB drastically reduces repetitive columnar data size
Automatic maintenance on CREATE, UPDATE, and DELETE with no intervention
EXPLAIN shows COLUMNAR strategy when planner detects equality or eligible aggregation
search_columnar_create_desc: Use DEFINE INDEX with the COLUMNAR keyword. The index accepts one or more table columns.
search_columnar_create_code:
DEFINE INDEX age_idx ON TABLE users COLUMNS age COLUMNAR;
DEFINE INDEX city_idx ON TABLE users COLUMNS city COLUMNAR;
search_columnar_agg_desc: The planner automatically detects aggregation functions with arguments on indexed columns and uses the columnar index instead of loading documents. The result is computed by scanning only the column bytes.
search_columnar_agg_code: SELECT count(), sum(age), avg(age) AS media, min(age), max(age) FROM users;
search_columnar_eq_desc: The columnar index also accelerates WHERE column = value queries. The sortable encoder produces an exact key, enabling direct seek on the CI| prefix without scanning the table.
search_columnar_eq_code:
SELECT * FROM users WHERE age = 25;
-- EXPLAIN shows: strategy: COLUMNAR, indexName: age_idx
search_columnar_when_desc: Use columnar indexes on tables with many rows (100K+) when you frequently run aggregations like dashboards, reports, or count/sum/avg/min/max queries. The gain is larger when indexed columns have numeric types or short strings with high repetition. Does not replace UNIQUE indexes for exact equality lookup in OLTP tables — use the appropriate index type for each query pattern. Unlike SEARCH, GEO, and HNSW indexes, the columnar index does not use approximate search or ranking: it is deterministic and serves pure analytical aggregation.

search_vector_python_sdk_desc: The axonbase Python SDK provides AxonBaseVectorStore for async vector operations.
search_vector_python_sdk_code:
from axonbase import Axon
from axonbase.vectorstore import AxonBaseVectorStore, VectorRecord

async def main():
    axon = await Axon.connect("ws://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc/ws")
    await axon.use("app", "main")

    store = AxonBaseVectorStore(
        axon=axon,
        collection="knowledge_chunks",
        dimensions=384,
        distance="cosine",
    )
    await store.ensure_schema()

    record = VectorRecord(
        id="doc1_chunk1",
        content="AxonBase suporta indices HNSW para busca vetorial ANN",
        embedding=[0.12, 0.45, 0.78, 0.33],
        metadata={"fonte": "s3://docs/manual.pdf", "pagina": 12},
        source_uri="s3://docs/manual.pdf",
        chunk_index=0,
    )
    await store.upsert([record])

    results = await store.similarity_search_by_vector(
        vector=[0.11, 0.44, 0.76, 0.35],
        limit=5,
    )
    for r in results:

dblink_intro: DATABASE LINK connects to remote AxonBase servers and makes their tables accessible as if they were local. Use the syntax "link_name"."table_name" in SELECT, JOIN, and subqueries. Tables without a prefix always resolve to the local database — existing queries work unchanged.
dblink_create_desc: Use DEFINE DATABASE LINK to register a remote server. Provide the WebSocket URL, namespace, database, and optional credentials. The link is stored in the catalog and replicated via Raft like any other DDL.
dblink_query_desc: Prefix the table name with the link name and a dot: "link_name"."table_name". All SELECT operations work: WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, GROUP BY, functions, graph traversals, and full-text/vector/geo search are pushed down to the remote server.
dblink_join_desc: JOIN any combination of local tables, link tables, and local qualified tables. When both sides of a JOIN are on the same link, the join is executed remotely (pushdown). When sides are on different links, results are fetched in parallel and joined locally.
dblink_join_code:
-- Local + remote JOIN
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM users u
JOIN "europe"."orders" o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.age > 25;

-- JOIN between two remote databases
SELECT e.name, a.name
FROM "europe"."customers" e
JOIN "asia"."customers" a ON e.email = a.email;

-- Two tables from the same link (pushdown)
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM "europe"."users" u
JOIN "europe"."orders" o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE u.age > 25;
dblink_drop_desc: Use DROP DATABASE LINK to remove a registered link. Connections to the remote server are closed. Queries referencing the link name will fail until the link is recreated.
dblink_performance_desc: DATABASE LINK uses HTTP POST to the remote server's /sql endpoint. Connections are pooled and reused. The query is sent as-is with the remote namespace and database headers — the remote server executes it natively. Pushdown optimizations (WHERE, LIMIT, ORDER BY, JOIN, GROUP BY) are applied automatically: if all referenced columns belong to the same link, the entire filtered query is sent remotely, minimizing data transfer. For JOINs across different links, results are fetched in parallel and processed locally.
dblink_notes_desc: DATABASE LINK accepts SELECT, CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, and RELATE. The link name is defined with DEFINE DATABASE LINK.
saga_intro: A SAGA coordinates changes across independent AxonBase databases. The orchestrator sends operations to participants and issues CANCEL SAGA when any step fails, triggering local compensation.
saga_architecture_desc: BEGIN SAGA, COMMIT SAGA, and CANCEL SAGA always go to the orchestrator. Each participant database runs its own local transaction.

saga_finish_desc: COMMIT SAGA closes the distributed transaction and keeps the changes. CANCEL SAGA rolls back every participant.

config_cert_login_code:
curl -k https://127.0.0.1:8443/certificate/login/icp_brasil?ns=test\&db=dev \
  --cert client.pem --key client.key
# Returns an axontc_ temporary credential, e.g.:
# {"credential":"axontc_...", "user":"12345678901", "expiresIn":60}

# Use the credential as password in signin:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/signin \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"user":"12345678901","pass":"axontc_..."}'
config_cert_rpc_desc: For applications that cannot present a certificate in a TLS handshake, use the certificate.begin and certificate.complete RPC flow. begin returns a 32-byte Base64URL challenge; sign the exact ASCII bytes with the client private key and send the DER Base64 certificate chain to complete.
config_cert_rpc_code:

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":1,"method":"certificate.begin","params":[{"store":"icp_brasil"}]}'
# -> {"id":"...","challenge":"<base64url>","expiresAt":"..."}

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/rpc \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"id":2,"method":"certificate.complete","params":[{"id":"...","challenge":"<same base64url>","store":"icp_brasil","user":"12345678901","chain":["<DER base64>"],"signature":"<base64>"}]}'
# -> { "credential": "axontc_...", "user": "12345678901" }

ai_audit_assign_desc: The AUDITED BY clause attaches the user to an audit. Only that user's commands pass through the materialized rules.
ai_audit_assign_code:
DEFINE USER alice ON DATABASE
  PASSWORD 'secret'
  ROLES editor
  AUDITED BY protect_production;
ai_audit_safe_desc: The command does not match a rule and runs normally.
ai_audit_warning_desc: The command remains pending until someone records an explicit decision.
ai_audit_danger_desc: The operation is rejected and the user stays blocked until authorization.
ai_audit_resolve_desc: Authorization executes the original SQL exactly once with an audit bypass, avoiding a second case for the same operation.
ai_audit_resolve_code:
SET REASON AUDIT CASE 'a8d4...' 'Cleanup approved for the maintenance window';
SET AUDIT CASE 'a8d4...' AUTHORIZED REASON 'Change registered in ticket OPS-218';
ai_audit_cases_desc: AUDIT_CASES is a virtual table with the original SQL, classification, user, reason, resolution, and case events.
ai_audit_diagram_footer: AI creates the rules. AxonBase makes every runtime decision.

use_cases_intro: From financial services to healthcare, AxonBase replaces multiple specialized systems with a single engine, reducing infrastructure complexity, operational cost, and security risk.
use_cases_positioning_text: AxonBase is the database for microservices and AI agents that need distributed transactions, AI governance, and multi-model search, all in a single SQL engine.

use_cases_positioning.title: What Makes AxonBase Different
use_cases_positioning.subtitle: Three capabilities that no other database combines in a single engine:
features: Distributed transactions via native sagas: BEGIN SAGA, COMMIT SAGA, CANCEL SAGA with correlation, compensation, and remote rollback
AI governance with AI Audit: LLM-generated rules classify every query as SAFE, WARNING, or DANGER before execution, without sending production data to the AI provider
Multi-model search in one engine: BM25 full-text, HNSW vectors, GeoJSON spatial, graph traversal, and columnar aggregation, all in a single AxonQL statement

use_cases_sectors_intro: Each sector benefits from a different combination of AxonBase capabilities. The engine adapts to the data shape, not the other way around.

use_cases_sectors.title: Banking and Financial Services
use_cases_sectors.pain: Banks need ACID transactions, audit trails, and role-based access across millions of accounts, with real-time fraud detection and strict regulatory compliance.
capabilities: Sagas for distributed ledger transactions across core banking systems, with automatic compensation on failure
Data Rules with field masking to protect PII (CPF, account numbers, credit cards) without modifying application code
AI Audit to classify every query as SAFE, WARNING, or DANGER before execution, meeting Bacen and LGPD requirements
mTLS and certificate-based authentication (ICP-Brasil compatible) for secure inter-bank communication
Columnar indexes for real-time aggregation of balances, transaction counts, and risk metrics without ETL

use_cases_sectors.title: Fintech and Payments
use_cases_sectors.pain: Fintechs move fast but cannot compromise on compliance. They need a database that supports rapid iteration, auditability, and multi-tenant isolation from day one.
capabilities: Multi-tenant by design: namespaces and databases isolate each client or product line with zero configuration
Graph relations for payment flows, wallet hierarchies, and recommendation networks in a single query
Live queries for real-time balance updates, transaction notifications, and fraud alerts over WebSocket
JDBC driver for existing BI tools, plus GraphQL and REST for mobile and web backends
Scalable from startup MVP to millions of users with the same RocksDB-backed engine

use_cases_sectors.title: Government and Public Sector
use_cases_sectors.pain: Governments require data sovereignty, auditability, and ICP-Brasil certificate support. They cannot afford vendor lock-in or cloud-only solutions.
capabilities: Certificate-based authentication with ICP-Brasil trust store for digital signatures and identity verification
AI Audit for automated compliance verification of every data access and modification
Data Rules with field masking to protect citizen PII across all queries without application changes
Self-hosted deployment with no cloud dependency: RocksDB persistence, S3 backup, and Raft cluster
Full audit trail via S3 backup encryption (AES-256-GCM) and export/import for data portability

use_cases_sectors.title: Healthtech and Healthcare
use_cases_sectors.pain: Healthcare applications handle sensitive patient data, require strict access control, and need to query structured records, clinical notes, and medical images in a compliant way.
capabilities: Data Rules with field masking to protect patient PII (name, CPF, diagnosis) without touching application code
AI Audit to classify every query and block unauthorized access to patient records
BM25 full-text search over clinical notes, prescriptions, and medical reports with relevance ranking
HNSW vector search for semantic similarity over medical embeddings and imaging metadata
Sagas for distributed healthcare workflows: appointment scheduling, lab results, and billing across systems

use_cases_sectors.title: E-Commerce and Marketplace
use_cases_sectors.pain: E-commerce platforms need real-time product search, personalized recommendations, inventory management, and order processing, all with high availability.
capabilities: BM25 full-text search for product catalogs with relevance ranking and highlighting
HNSW vector search for semantic product recommendations and visual similarity
Graph traversal for recommendation networks: customers who bought X also bought Y
Geo search for local inventory, store locators, and delivery radius queries
Live queries for real-time inventory updates, order status changes, and price alerts via WebSocket

use_cases_sectors.title: IoT and Telemetry
use_cases_sectors.pain: IoT systems ingest millions of data points per second, need time-series aggregation, geospatial queries, and real-time alerting with minimal operational overhead.
capabilities: Columnar indexes for real-time aggregation of count, sum, avg, min, max over sensor data without loading raw documents
Geo search for location-based queries: devices within a radius, fleet tracking, geofence alerts
Live queries for real-time telemetry streaming and threshold alerts over WebSocket
Raft cluster for high availability and automatic failover in distributed sensor networks
RocksDB storage for high-ingestion throughput (243K inserts/s in batch)

use_cases_sectors.title: Legal and Compliance
use_cases_sectors.pain: Legal departments manage contracts, litigation documents, and regulatory filings that require full-text search, version history, and strict access control.
capabilities: BM25 full-text search over legal documents with configurable analyzers, stopwords, and stemming
Data Rules to enforce attorney-client privilege and document-level access control
AI Audit to classify queries and prevent unauthorized access to sensitive legal content
Sagas for distributed contract lifecycle management: drafting, review, approval, and signing
Export/import for data portability and archival compliance
